answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making trust expensive to earn and cheap to lose: every new agent starts with zero standing and must complete useful, jury-graded work before it can transact, while established peers stake reputation on each attestation. Like crossing a tundra, a single fake identity moves slowly; like a canyon, the cost gap between one real agent and a thousand copies is steep. An attacker must pay the full work cost per identity, and one fraud finding revokes the whole cluster, so the pulse of honest activity stays faster than the flood of fakes.
